claim: Spo11 initiates meiotic recombination by forming DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs).
source: Meiotic recombination is initiated by programmed DNA double-strand break (DSB) formation by the transesterase Spo11 (Keeney et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Keeney et al., 1997.

claim: At least 10 additional factors are required for Spo11-dependent DSB activity.
source: In addition to Spo11, at least 10 additional factors are required for Spo11-dependent DSB activity, and collectively these factors are referred to as the meiotic DSB machinery.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text based on established knowledge.

claim: Mer2 was originally identified as a high-copy number suppressor of the mer1 phenotype.
source: This protein (also known as Rec107) was originally identified as a high-copy number suppressor of the mer1 phenotype (Mer1 was later shown to be a cofactor for the splicing of various meiotic mRNAs, including Mer2; Engebrecht et al., 1991), after which it was shown to be essential for meiosis (Engebrecht et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Engebrecht et al., 1991 and 1990.

claim: Mer2 is essential for meiosis.
source: This protein (also known as Rec107) was originally identified as a high-copy number suppressor of the mer1 phenotype (Mer1 was later shown to be a cofactor for the splicing of various meiotic mRNAs, including Mer2; Engebrecht et al., 1991), after which it was shown to be essential for meiosis (Engebrecht et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Engebrecht et al., 1990.

claim: Mer2 is the target of S-Cdk and DDK (Cdc7-Dbf4) phosphorylation.
source: Mer2 is central to the temporal control of Spo11-dependent DSB formation, being the target of S-Cdk and DDK (Cdc7-Dbf4) phosphorylation that presumably allows the binding of the Spo11-associated factors Rec114 and Mei4 to Mer2 (Matos et al., 2008; Murakami and Keeney, 2014; Wan et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Matos et al., 2008; Murakami and Keeney, 2014; Wan et al., 2008.

claim: Mer2 forms a complex with Rec114-Mei4.
source: In addition to forming a complex with Rec114-Mei4, Mer2 interacts directly with the PHD domain-containing protein Spp1 (Acquaviva et al., 2013; Sommermeyer et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text.

claim: Mer2 interacts directly with the PHD domain-containing protein Spp1.
source: In addition to forming a complex with Rec114-Mei4, Mer2 interacts directly with the PHD domain-containing protein Spp1 (Acquaviva et al., 2013; Sommermeyer et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Acquaviva et al., 2013; Sommermeyer et al., 2013.

claim: Spp1 binds to nucleosomes that are tri- (or di-) methylated on H3K4.
source: Spp1 binds to nucleosomes that are tri- (or di-) methylated on H3K4 (i.e. H3K4me3 nucleosomes) (He et al., 2019; Miller et al., 2001), and this association is important for the association of Spo11-dependent DSB formation with gene promoter regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to He et al., 2019; Miller et al., 2001.

claim: The C-terminal region of Spp1 interacts with a central, predicted coiled-coil, region of Mer2.
source: The C-terminal region of Spp1 interacts with a central, predicted coiled-coil, region of Mer2 (Acquaviva et al., 2013; Sommermeyer et al., 2013; Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Acquaviva et al., 2013; Sommermeyer et al., 2013 and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: A single amino acid substitution in Mer2 (V195D) is sufficient to disrupt the interaction with Spp1.
source: A single amino acid substitution in Mer2 (V195D) is sufficient to disrupt the interaction with Spp1 (as judged by yeast-2-hybrid [Y2H] analysis) (Adam et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Adam et al., 2018.

claim: Spp1 associated with Mer2 has a longer residence time on nucleosomes when compared with Spp1 when part of COMPASS.
source: Interestingly, Spp1 associated with Mer2 has a longer residence time on nucleosomes when compared with Spp1 when part of COMPASS (Karányi et al., 2018), suggesting additional functions for Mer2 in mediating nucleosome tethering.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Karányi et al., 2018.

claim: mer2Δ cells completely fail to form meiotic DSBs.
source: In line with the central position for Mer2 in DSB machinery assembly is the observation that – in contrast to deletion of Set1 or Spp1 which severely reduces, but not eliminates DSB formation – mer2Δ cells completely fail to form meiotic DSBs (Rockmill et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rockmill et al., 1995.

claim: Homologs of Mer2 in fission yeast and mouse interact with meiotic chromosome axis-associated HORMA proteins.
source: For example, homologs of Mer2 in fission yeast (Kariyazono et al., 2019) and mouse (Stanzione et al., 2016) interact with meiotic chromosome axis-associated HORMA proteins, suggesting that Mer2 can mediate a link between the chromosome axis (via HORMA protein interaction) and chromatin loops (through Spp1 association).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kariyazono et al., 2019 and Stanzione et al., 2016.

claim: Mer2 and Spp1 can be co-purified to homogeneity and free of nucleic acid contamination.
source: In co-lysis experiments, we found that we could purify a complex of Mer2 and Spp1 to homogeneity, and free of nucleic acid contamination (Mer2FL with Spp1 shown as an example in Figure 1C, note the apparent A260 to A280 ratio as evidence of a lack of nucleic acid contamination), thus indicating that the interaction between Mer2 and Spp1 does not require any PTMs or additional cofactors and that the interaction was robust enough to survive extensive co-purification in >300 mM NaCl.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The interaction between Mer2 and Spp1 does not require any PTMs or additional cofactors.
source: In co-lysis experiments, we found that we could purify a complex of Mer2 and Spp1 to homogeneity, and free of nucleic acid contamination (Mer2FL with Spp1 shown as an example in Figure 1C, note the apparent A260 to A280 ratio as evidence of a lack of nucleic acid contamination), thus indicating that the interaction between Mer2 and Spp1 does not require any PTMs or additional cofactors and that the interaction was robust enough to survive extensive co-purification in >300 mM NaCl.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the successful purification of the complex without additional factors.

claim: Spp1 binds Mer2FL with a KD of 24 nM (±2).
source: Spp1 bound Mer2FL with a KD of 24 nM (±2), and to Mer2Core with a KD of 137 nM (±4).
evidence: The claim is supported by MST experimental data.

claim: Spp1 binds Mer2Core with a KD of 137 nM (±4).
source: Spp1 bound Mer2FL with a KD of 24 nM (±2), and to Mer2Core with a KD of 137 nM (±4).
evidence: The claim is supported by MST experimental data.

claim: The majority of the Spp1 binding interface is within the core of Mer2.
source: Thus, we confirm that the majority of the Spp1 binding interface is indeed within the core of Mer2, as reported earlier (Acquaviva et al., 2013; Adam et al., 2018), although there does appear to be some contribution to Spp1 binding provided by the N- and C-terminal regions of Mer2.
evidence: The claim is supported by MST data and citations to Acquaviva et al., 2013; Adam et al., 2018.

claim: Mer2core is the tetramerisation region.
source: We measured the molecular mass of Mer2 by size exclusion chromatography coupled to multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS) and concluded that Mer2core is the tetramerisation region (Figure 1E, orange trace and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-D), consistent with recent observations of Mer2 (Claeys Bouuaert et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-D, and a citation to Claeys Bouuaert et al., 2021.

claim: The Mer2 tetramer binds two copies of Spp1, establishing a complex in a 4:2 stoichiometry.
source: Taken together we conclude that the Mer2 tetramer binds two copies of Spp1, establishing a complex in a 4:2 stoichiometry.
evidence: The claim is supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: Mer2 mediates the dimerisation of Spp1.
source: Thus we show a novel function for Mer2 in not simply binding Spp1, but importantly, in mediating the dimerisation of Spp1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the 4:2 stoichiometry data.

claim: The Mer2-Spp1 assembly binds more tightly to nucleosomes compared to monomeric Spp1 alone.
source: We observed that the Mer2-Spp1 assembly (in which two copies of Spp1 are present) bound more tightly to nucleosomes, as compared to monomeric Spp1 alone (which bound relatively weakly to nucleosomes, consistent with the reported ~1 µM affinity of the PHD domain with H3K4me3 peptide; He et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA and pulldown data, and a citation to He et al., 2019.

claim: GST-Spp1 exhibits an intermediate apparent binding affinity to nucleosomes compared to Spp1:Mer2 and Spp1 alone.
source: Interestingly, when we compared the observed binding of Spp1:Mer2 with GST-Spp1, we found that GST-Spp1 exhibited an intermediate apparent binding affinity.
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA and pulldown data.

claim: Mer2 directly contributes to nucleosome binding in addition to triggering Spp1 'dimerisation'.
source: A potential corollary of this observation is that Mer2 in addition to triggering Spp1 'dimerisation' might directly contribute to nucleosome binding.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of binding affinities.

claim: Most of the cross-links between the Mer2-Spp1 complex and the nucleosomes are via regions of Mer2.
source: Most strikingly however, the cross-linking revealed that most of the cross-links between the Mer2-Spp1 complex and the nucleosomes are via regions of Mer2, in the N-term, core, and C-term regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by XL-MS data.

claim: The cross-links between Mer2-Spp1 and nucleosomes cluster around histone H3 and the DNA entry/exit site on the nucleosomes.
source: We observe that the cross-links cluster around histone H3, but more generally around the DNA entry/exit site on the nucleosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by XL-MS data modeled onto nucleosome structure.

claim: Mer2FL binds to unmodified mononucleosomes.
source: We tested whether Mer2FL could bind to unmodified mononucleosomes in an SEC experiment, and surprisingly found that it formed a stable complex (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by SEC data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mer2 binds to mononucleosomes with a 4:1 stoichiometry.
source: In MP, we observe a mix of three species, free Mer2 tetramer (measured at 127 kDa; theoretical mass 142 kDa), free mononucleosomes (measured at 187 kDa; theoretical mass 202 kDa), and a complex at 303 kDa, which most likely corresponds to a 4:1 complex of Mer2:nucleosomes (theoretical mass 344 kDa) (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass photometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Mer2 binds with a 6-fold higher apparent affinity to nucleosomes (5 nM) than to the same 167 bp DNA used to reconstitute the nucleosomes (30 nM).
source: Using analytical EMSAs we found that Mer2 binds with a 6-fold higher apparent affinity to nucleosomes (5 nM vs. 30 nM) than to the same 167 bp DNA used to reconstitute the nucleosomes (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The main nucleosome interaction region of Mer2 lies in the C-terminal 58 amino acids.
source: We confirmed that the Mer2core did not bind nucleosomes, but neither did Mer2∆C, strongly suggesting that the main nucleosome interaction region of Mer2 lies in the C-terminal 58 amino acids (Figure 3F), with some additional contribution from the N-terminus of Mer2 (summarised in Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by pulldown data shown in Figure 3F and summarized in Figure 3G.

claim: Mer2 provides a direct binding interface with nucleosomes in addition to enabling the 'dimerisation' of Spp1.
source: We propose that Mer2, in addition to enabling the 'dimerisation' of Spp1 via its central tetramerisation domain, provides a direct binding interface with nucleosomes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the nucleosome binding data.

claim: Hop1 can exist in two topological states ('open/unbuckled' or 'closed').
source: Hop1 (like most other known HORMA domains) can exist in two topological states ('open/unbuckled' [O/U] or 'closed' [C]), in which the closed state can embrace a binding partner via a closed HORMA-closure motif 'safety belt' binding architecture (West et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to West et al., 2018.

claim: Meiotic HORMA proteins contain a CM at the end of their own C-terminus.
source: The meiotic HORMA proteins are unique among HORMA proteins in the fact that they contain a CM at the end of their own C-terminus (Hop1 residues 585–605; West et al., 2018), endowing these factors with the ability to form an intramolecular (closed) HORMA-CM configuration.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to West et al., 2018.

claim: The CM of Red1 binds to Hop1 with a higher affinity than the CM of Hop1.
source: The CM of Red1 (located 340–362; West et al., 2018) binds to Hop1 with a higher affinity than the CM of Hop1 (West et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to West et al., 2018.

claim: Mer2 binding to Hop1 is increased ~6-fold when Hop1 is co-expressed with Red1I743R-MBP compared to Hop1 alone.
source: We quantitated the Mer2 intensity relative to the Hop1 band in both pulldowns, and from three independent experiments, and observed an ~6-fold increase in Mer2 binding (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by pulldown data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mer2 does not have significant affinity for Red1.
source: We detected no Mer2 interaction when pulling on Red1I743R-MBP in the absence of Hop1. As such, we conclude that Mer2 does not have significant affinity for Red1.
evidence: The claim is supported by pulldown data.

claim: Hop1K593A has ~2-fold stronger binding to Mer2 than does Hop1WT.
source: Quantification of the pulldown analyses showed that Hop1K593A has ~2-fold stronger binding to Mer2 than does Hop1WT (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by pulldown data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Mer2 binding to Hop1 is driven largely by HORMA domain-mediated interactions.
source: Based on these data, and taking into consideration the effect of Red1 on the Hop1-Mer2 interaction, we suggest the following model: Mer2 binding to Hop1 is driven largely by HORMA domain-mediated interactions, and promoted under conditions where the HORMA is not bound to its intramolecular CM.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the pulldown data and the effect of Red1.

claim: Mer23A and Mer24A mutants failed to restore spore viability in mer2Δ.
source: Strikingly, expression of Mer23A-3HA or Mer24A-3HA failed to restore spore viability in mer2Δ; these strains essentially behaved indistinguishably from the mer2Δ strain.
evidence: The claim is supported by spore viability data.

claim: Expression of the Mer23A/4A mutants prevented the appearance of the phosphorylated version of histone H3-threonine 11.
source: When we probed for the activation of Mek1 kinase, which is regulated by DSB-dependent Mec1/Tel1 activation (Chuang et al., 2012; Niu et al., 2005), we noticed that expression of the Mer23A/4A mutants (in contrast to wildtype Mer2) prevented the appearance of the phosphorylated version of histone H3-threonine 11, a bona-fide Mek1 substrate (Kniewel et al., 2017; Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B and citations to Chuang et al., 2012; Niu et al., 2005; Kniewel et al., 2017.

claim: Expression of Mer23A/4A mutants did not support the phosphorylation of Hop1.
source: Together with the fact that expression of Mer23A/4A mutants did not support the phosphorylation of Hop1 (mediated by Mec1/Tel1 as a response to DSBs) (Carballo et al., 2008; Figure 5B; as seen by an apparent electrophoretic shift in Hop1), these data show that the expression of our Mer2 mutants leads to defective Mec1/Tel1-Mek1 signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B and a citation to Carballo et al., 2008.

claim: The recruitment of Mer2 to defined chromosomal foci was not disrupted in Mer23A and Mer24A expressing situations.
source: We found that the recruitment of Mer2 to defined chromosomal foci was not disrupted in Mer23A and Mer24A expressing situations (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by chromosome spread data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The biggest change in the Mer24A mutant vs. Mer2WT is a reduced binding to Hht1 (histone H3).
source: In summary, the biggest change we see in the Mer24A mutant vs. Mer2WT is a reduced binding to Hht1 (histone H3).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative IP-MS data.

claim: Interaction with Hop1 was largely unaffected in Mer24A compared to Mer2WT.
source: Interaction with Hop1 was largely unaffected (Figure 5G) – in agreement with our in vitro analysis (Figure 4E), as was association with Spp1 and Red1; the latter presumably associated via association with Hop1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by IP-MS data shown in Figure 5G and in vitro data in Figure 4E.

claim: A clear difference in binding between Mer2 and Mre11 was observed when comparing MER2 to the mer2-3a or mer2-4a mutants in Y2H analysis.
source: Nonetheless, we observed a clear difference in binding between the Mer2 and Mre11 when comparing MER2 to the mer2-3a or mer2-4a mutants (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by Y2H data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mer2 directly associates with Mre11.
source: We detected a robust interaction between Mer2WT and Mre11, and in line with our earlier result, we observed a reduced interaction between Mre11 and Mer2 when Mer23A and Mer24A were used in the pulldown assay (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by pulldown data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Mer23A leads to a 2-fold reduction in binding to Mre11.
source: We quantified the amount of Mer2 in the pulldown as a factor of Mre11 (Figure 6C): Mer23A leads to a 2-fold reduction in binding, and Mer24A a reduction closer to 10-fold.
evidence: The claim is supported by pulldown data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Mer24A leads to a reduction closer to 10-fold in binding to Mre11.
source: We quantified the amount of Mer2 in the pulldown as a factor of Mre11 (Figure 6C): Mer23A leads to a 2-fold reduction in binding, and Mer24A a reduction closer to 10-fold.
evidence: The claim is supported by pulldown data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Mer23A and Mer24A disrupt a key functionality of Mer2 that is required for meiotic DSB formation.
source: We detected a strong impairment of meiotic DSB activity specifically in mer2-3a or mer2-4a, to an extent that was comparable to what was observed in mer2Δ strains (Figure 6E). Thus, Mer23A and Mer24A disrupt a key functionality of Mer2 that is required for meiotic DSB formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by Southern blot data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The interaction between Spp1 and Mer2 is tight (~25 nM) and not dependent on any post-translational modification or additional cofactors.
source: The interaction between Spp1 and Mer2 is tight (~25 nM) and not dependent on any post-translational modification or additional cofactors.
evidence: The claim is supported by MST data.

claim: Mer2 serves as a dimerisation platform for Spp1, effectively increasing its affinity for H3K4me3 nucleosomes.
source: Importantly, we also find that Mer2 serves as a dimerisation platform for Spp1, effectively increasing its affinity for H3K4me3 nucleosomes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the stoichiometry and binding data.

claim: Mer2 itself is a bona-fide nucleosome binder.
source: We find that Mer2 itself is a bona-fide nucleosome binder.
evidence: The claim is supported by SEC, mass photometry, and EMSA data.

claim: Mer2 binds to nucleosomal DNA.
source: Given that Mer2 has been previously shown to bind DNA (Claeys Bouuaert et al., 2021), yet still binds to an NCP (with 147 bp DNA and no DNA overhangs), and that neither the loss of histone tails nor the acidic patch mutant disrupted the interaction, we suggest that Mer2 binds to nucleosomal DNA.
evidence: The claim is inferred from EMSA data and a citation to Claeys Bouuaert et al., 2021.

claim: The direct interaction between Mer2 and Mre11, via conserved residues in Mer2, is a universal feature of the meiotic program.
source: Importantly, the residues that are mutated in Mer23A are essentially universally conserved throughout the eukaryotic kingdom (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). As such, we surmise that the direct interaction between Mer2 and Mre11, via these residues, is a universal feature of the meiotic program.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the conservation of residues shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mer2 forms the keystone of meiotic recombination, binding directly to the axis via Hop1 and to the loop via nucleosomes.
source: Taken together our data show that Mer2 forms the keystone of meiotic recombination, binding directly to the axis – via Hop1-, and to the loop – via nucleosomes.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference from all the data presented.

claim: The N-terminus of Mer2 recruits the MRX complex via Mre11, a step that is critical for the formation of meiotic DSBs and the successful completion of meiosis.
source: Simultaneously, our data indicate that the N-terminus of Mer2 recruits the MRX complex via Mre11, a step that we suggest is critical for the formation of meiotic DSBs and the successful completion of meiosis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the Y2H, pulldown, and DSB formation data.
